overview: This was a proposed "rule," a House resolution that sets the terms for debating other legislation. It would have set up votes on two resolutions canceling Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rules on overdraft fees at very large banks and on supervising large digital payment apps, plus debate on H.R. 1526, limiting federal district courts' power to issue injunctions that block government actions, and H.R. 22, requiring proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections. It also would have set aside House Resolutions 23 and 164 and barred "discharge petitions," a tool that lets a majority of members force a floor vote, on measures substantially the same as House Resolution 23. On April 1, 2025, the House voted it down; a revised rule, House Resolution 294, was adopted a week later.
for: Supporters say the rule would have moved several priority bills to a vote efficiently and kept the floor schedule under the control of House leadership.
against: Critics say it went beyond scheduling by blocking members from using a discharge petition, a long-standing way for a majority to force a vote, and bundled unrelated bills under tight debate limits.
